findings.observation: Reviewed supplementary document 'Traffic Impact Analysis Determination' (documentId: be3343ae-a570-434f-8f82-a7e396bcc27b). Section 3 'TPW Staff Determination' shows checkbox marked '[X] A traffic impact analysis is NOT required' with reviewer Manar Hasan dated 3/19/2026. The determination explicitly states 'Traffic generated by the proposal does not exceed thresholds established in the City of Austin Land Development Code (LDC).'
findings.reasoning: The checklist item asks whether a TIA report is missing when the TIA Determination indicates it is required. The condition states 'If TIA required per worksheet (generally >2,000 trips/day)'. The TIA Determination Worksheet clearly indicates a TIA is NOT required. Therefore, the condition for this checklist item is not met, making it not applicable.
findings.explanation: TIA Determination Worksheet indicates TIA is not required for this project.

findings.observation: Used vision_check on Sheet 13 (Overall Site & Paving & Striping Plan) to examine driveway locations along Collier Street and South Lamar Boulevard. Vision analysis found two driveways on Collier Street labeled 'TYPE II DRIVEWAY SEE SHEET 30 FOR DETAILS' and one on South Lamar Boulevard. No dimension lines or text indicating spacing distances between driveways or from driveways to intersections were found. Also checked Sheet 14 (Dimensional Control & Site Plan) - no driveway spacing dimensions shown there either.
findings.reasoning: The checklist item states 'Driveway spacing dimensions not shown on plans'. The vision analysis confirms this deficiency exists - while driveways are depicted on the plans, the spacing dimensions required for review are missing. The plans reference detail Sheet 30 for driveway construction details, but spacing dimensions should appear on the site plan layout sheets themselves per standard practice.
findings.explanation: Driveway spacing dimensions are not shown on site plan sheets 13 or 14.
findings.resolution: Add dimension lines showing driveway spacing from adjacent driveways and from nearest intersections on the site plan.

findings.observation: Used vision_check on Sheet 13 to examine driveway details. Vision analysis found two driveways on Collier Street with callouts reading 'TYPE II DRIVEWAY SEE SHEET 30 FOR DETAILS' and 'TYPE I DRIVEWAY SEE SHEET 30 FOR DETAILS', and one driveway on South Lamar Boulevard labeled 'TYPE II DRIVEWAY'. No explicit driveway width dimensions or curb return radii are shown on Sheet 13 itself - these details are deferred to Sheet 30 which contains standard construction details.
findings.reasoning: The checklist item asks if 'Driveway widths or curb return radii not shown on plans'. While Sheet 30 contains standard driveway details, the site plan layout sheets (13, 14) do not show the actual widths and curb return radii for the specific driveways on this project. Standard practice requires these dimensions to be shown on the site plan to demonstrate compliance with spacing and geometric requirements specific to this site's conditions.
findings.explanation: Driveway widths and curb return radii dimensions are not shown on site plan sheets.
findings.resolution: Add driveway width and curb return radii dimensions on the site plan for each proposed driveway.

findings.observation: Used vision_check on Sheet 13 to identify adjacent driveways within 300 feet. Vision analysis found that while some adjacent driveways are visually depicted on neighboring properties along South Lamar Boulevard (near South Place Condominiums) and Collier Street (Rogers Wilson Subdivision properties), there are no dimensions, distance labels, or a clearly marked 300-foot radius zone to demonstrate that all adjacent driveways within the required 300-foot distance have been comprehensively documented.
findings.reasoning: The checklist item requires that 'Adjacent driveways within 300 feet' be shown on plans. The validation methodology notes that vision should be used to 'look for adjacent driveways' and identify them. While the plan shows some adjacent driveways, it lacks the dimensions or demarcation needed to verify compliance with the 300-foot requirement. Without distance indicators, reviewers cannot confirm all adjacent driveways within the threshold have been identified.
findings.explanation: Adjacent driveways are depicted but not dimensioned; no 300-foot radius shown to verify compliance.
findings.resolution: Show all adjacent driveways within 300 feet of proposed driveways with dimension lines indicating distances, or show a 300-foot radius zone.

findings.observation: The condition states 'If site fronts undivided street'. From facts.md, Collier Street is classified as '2U-OP (2-lane undivided)' while S Lamar Boulevard is '4D (4-lane divided)'. Used vision_check on Sheet 13 to examine Collier Street frontage. Vision analysis found two proposed driveways on Collier Street (labeled 'TYPE II DRIVEWAY SEE SHEET 30 FOR DETAILS'). Properties on the opposite (north) side of Collier Street are identified, but no dimension lines are drawn across the street to indicate offset distances between the proposed driveways and any opposing driveways on the north side.
findings.reasoning: The condition is met (site fronts Collier Street, an undivided street), making this item applicable. The checklist item asks if 'Offsets from opposing driveways not dimensioned on undivided street frontage'. The vision analysis confirms this deficiency - while the plan shows both sides of Collier Street, offset dimensions between opposing driveways are not provided, which are needed to verify adequate spacing and sight distance per transportation standards.
findings.explanation: Site fronts undivided Collier Street; offset dimensions from opposing driveways are not shown.
findings.resolution: Add dimension lines showing offsets between proposed driveways on Collier Street and any opposing driveways on the north side of the street.

findings.observation: Reviewed Sheet 16 blocks.md which contains the '1700 SOUTH LAMAR - PARKING TABLE'. The table includes a 'PROPOSED USE-MIX' column showing: STUDIO (70 units), 1 BEDROOM (328 units), 2 BEDROOM (55 units), 3 BEDROOM (6 units), RESTAURANT (4,888 SF), RETAIL (GENERAL) (5,046 SF), and LEASING OFFICE (5,661 SF). The residential uses show unit counts while commercial uses show square footage.
findings.reasoning: The checklist item asks if the parking table fails to show 'proposed land use(s) with square footage'. The table clearly shows all proposed land uses. For commercial uses (restaurant, retail, leasing office), square footage is provided. For residential uses, unit counts are shown, which is the standard metric for residential parking calculations. This satisfies the requirement to identify land uses and their quantification for parking analysis.
findings.explanation: Parking table on Sheet 16 shows all proposed land uses with square footage (commercial) and units (residential).

findings.observation: Reviewed Sheet 16 parking table in blocks.md which shows 'TOTAL PRIVATE PARKING SPACES PROVIDED: 647'. Used vision_check on Sheet 16 to verify bicycle parking counts. Vision analysis confirmed the parking table shows bicycle parking with 'LONG TERM PROVIDED: 44' and 'SHORT TERM PROVIDED: 24'. Sheet 16 guide.md also lists 'Total Private Parking Provided: 647 spaces' in the key values section.
findings.reasoning: The checklist item asks if 'Total number of provided parking spaces (vehicle and bicycle) not shown'. The parking table clearly displays the total vehicle parking (647 spaces) and both long-term (44) and short-term (24) bicycle parking provided counts. This satisfies the requirement to show total parking provisions for both vehicle and bicycle spaces.
findings.explanation: Total parking shown: 647 vehicle spaces, 44 long-term bicycle, 24 short-term bicycle on Sheet 16.

findings.observation: Reviewed Sheet 37 (Building Plan - Level 1) guide.md which lists parking space dimensions: Regular Parking Space 9'-0" x 17'-0", Compact Parking Space 7'-6" x 16'-0", Accessible Parking Space 8'-0" x 18'-0" with 5'-0" aisle, Van Accessible Parking Space 16'-0" x 18'-0" with 5'-0" aisle. Also reviewed Sheet 37 blocks.md Block 2 (Symbol Legend) which shows the same dimensions with typical depth dimensions of 18'-0" for regular/accessible and 16'-0" for compact, and width dimensions.
findings.reasoning: The checklist item asks if 'Parking stall width, depth, or angle not dimensioned'. Sheet 37's parking garage legend clearly provides width, depth (length), and aisle dimensions for all parking space types. While angles are not explicitly stated numerically, the plan drawings show the stall orientations. The key dimensional requirements (width and depth) are documented, which is sufficient for completeness review of parking layout compliance.
findings.explanation: Parking stall widths and depths are dimensioned in the parking garage legend on Sheet 37.

findings.observation: Used vision_check on Sheet 37 (Building Plan - Level 1) to examine parking aisle widths. Vision analysis found that while the floor plan layout itself does not have explicit dimension lines drawn across circulation aisles, the 'SYMBOL LEGEND' in the top right corner includes a diagram labeled 'TRAFFIC COATING AREA' that shows a typical parking layout with an aisle width dimension reading '24'-0" TYP (MIN)'.
findings.reasoning: The checklist item asks if 'Parking aisle widths or internal driveway widths not dimensioned'. While the dimension is shown in the legend rather than on the plan layout itself, the typical aisle width of 24'-0" minimum is documented on the sheet. This provides the required information for parking aisle compliance review. For a completeness check, providing the dimension in the legend is acceptable as long as the information is present and accessible to reviewers.
findings.explanation: Parking aisle width of 24'-0" typical minimum is shown in the parking garage legend on Sheet 37.

findings.observation: Used vision_check on Sheet 37 to examine how parking spaces are identified. Vision analysis confirmed that individual parking stalls throughout the parking garage are explicitly labeled with type designators: 'R' for regular, 'C' for compact, 'HC' for accessible handicapped, 'VAN' for van accessible, 'R-EVR' for EV ready, and 'R-EV' for EV charging installed. The 'PARKING GARAGE LEGEND' on the same sheet defines each of these codes with full descriptions and dimensions.
findings.reasoning: The checklist item asks if 'Parking spaces not identified by type (standard, compact, handicapped, bicycle)'. The vision analysis clearly shows that parking spaces ARE identified by type using letter codes on the plan, with a corresponding legend. This allows reviewers to verify the parking type distribution matches the parking table requirements. The spaces are properly identified on the plans.
findings.explanation: Parking spaces are identified by type using letter codes (R, C, HC, VAN) on Sheet 37 plans.

findings.observation: Used vision_check on Sheet 13 (Overall Site & Paving & Striping Plan) which shows 'PROPOSED ADA PATH' connecting public sidewalks, building perimeter, courtyard, and bicycle parking. However, the plan references 'SEE ARCHITECTURAL PLANS FOR DETAILS' for the parking garage, so connection to accessible parking cannot be verified from Sheet 13. Used vision_check on Sheet 37 (Building Plan - Level 1) which shows HC and VAN parking spaces with physical crossing paths drawn using solid lines. The Symbol Legend defines an 'ACCESSIBLE ROUTE' using a specific dashed line symbol, but this symbol is NOT shown on the paths connecting accessible parking spaces to building entrances and elevators.
findings.reasoning: The checklist item asks if 'Accessible route of travel not shown connecting all accessible elements'. Sheet 13 shows exterior accessible paths but cannot verify the critical connection to the parking garage. Sheet 37 shows physical paths from accessible parking but fails to mark them with the 'ACCESSIBLE ROUTE' symbol defined in its own legend. The accessible route must be explicitly and consistently shown connecting ALL accessible elements including parking, building entrances, and vertical circulation. The missing accessible route designation in the parking garage represents a gap in demonstrating ADA compliance.
findings.explanation: Accessible route symbol not shown connecting accessible parking spaces in garage to building entrances on Sheet 37.
findings.resolution: Add the accessible route designation (dashed line per legend) on Sheet 37 connecting HC/VAN parking spaces to building entrances and elevators.

findings.observation: Used vision_check on Sheet 13 to examine ramp locations where the 'PROPOSED ADA PATH' crosses vehicular ways. Vision analysis found that graphical representations of curb ramps (shown as rectangular hatched areas indicating tactile warning surfaces) ARE visible at transitions where the accessible path crosses driveways on Collier Street. Specifically, ramps are shown at the western driveway entrance (both sides) and at the mid-block crosswalk connection to the north side of Collier Street. While not explicitly labeled with text tags such as 'Ramp', the standard graphical representation is present.
findings.reasoning: The checklist item asks if 'Ramps connecting accessible elements not shown on plans'. The vision analysis confirms that ramps ARE shown graphically at the required transitions and curb cuts. Standard engineering practice uses hatched rectangles to denote curb ramps with tactile warning surfaces. The absence of text labels does not negate the fact that the ramps are depicted using standard symbology. The graphical representation is sufficient for completeness review to verify ramps are planned at appropriate locations.
findings.explanation: Curb ramps are shown graphically with hatched rectangles at accessible path transitions on Sheet 13.

findings.observation: The condition states 'If proposing off-site parking'. Reviewed Sheet 16 parking table which shows 'TOTAL PRIVATE PARKING SPACES PROVIDED: 647' and a column labeled 'COLLIER PUBLIC PARALLEL PARKING'. Reviewed Sheet 37 (Building Plan - Level 1) which shows all parking is provided in the parking garage within the building structure. Used semantic-search-blocks to search for 'off-site parking pedestrian ramp walking distance' but found no references to off-site parking facilities. The parallel parking on Collier Street appears to be on-street public parking, not off-site parking used to meet project parking requirements.
findings.reasoning: Off-site parking per LDC § 25-6-501 refers to parking located on a separate parcel that is used to meet the parking requirements for the development. All 647 parking spaces are shown as being provided on-site within the parking garage. The Collier Street parallel parking is public on-street parking, not off-site private parking. Since the project is not proposing off-site parking to meet its parking requirements, the condition for this item is not met.
findings.explanation: Project provides all required parking on-site in parking garage; no off-site parking proposed.

findings.observation: The condition states 'If proposing off-site parking'. Reviewed Sheet 16 parking table showing 647 total private parking spaces provided on-site. Reviewed Sheet 37 showing parking garage within the building structure. Used semantic-search-blocks to search for off-site parking references with no results indicating off-site parking facilities. All parking appears to be provided on-site within the development parcel.
findings.reasoning: Same rationale as OSP-01. The project is not proposing off-site parking per LDC § 25-6-501 to meet parking requirements. All 647 required parking spaces are shown within the on-site parking garage. Without off-site parking being proposed, there are no walking distances to dimension between off-site parking facilities and the use served. The condition for applicability is not met.
findings.explanation: No off-site parking proposed; all parking provided on-site within building.
